title: US Stock Market Today S&P 500 Futures Inch Higher As Inflation Worries Ease
content:
Find winning stocks in any market cycle. Join 7 million investors using Simply Wall St's investing ideas for FREE.

The Morning Bull - US Market Morning Update Thursday, May, 7 2026

US stock futures are slightly higher this morning, with E-mini S&P 500 contracts up about 0.1%, as investors balance cooler bond markets, cheaper oil, and fresh US jobs data. The US 10 year Treasury yield is holding near 4.35%, which means borrowing costs for mortgages and companies remain relatively elevated but are not climbing further for now. Hopes of a US Iran peace deal are pulling oil prices lower and easing some inflation worries, a key watchpoint for transport, airlines, and consumer focused stocks. At the same time, ADP shows 109,000 new private sector jobs in April 2026, the strongest reading since January 2025, which hints at a jobs market that is still adding workers. The big question for investors is whether this mix of steady hiring and softer inflation pressures keeps the pressure on interest rate sensitive areas like banks and real estate or continues to favor growth heavy sectors such as technology and smaller company indexes.

title: Did Oppenheimer’s ABNB Upgrade and AI Focus Just Shift Airbnb’s Investment Narrative?
content:
In recent days, Airbnb has attracted attention as Oppenheimer upgraded the company to Outperform and analysts projected higher year-over-year earnings and revenue ahead of its Q1 2026 report, even as insider share sales and geopolitical risks around travel persisted. At the same time, Airbnb’s push into hotels, Reserve Now Pay Later, AI-powered search, and its FIFA World Cup 2026 partnership are emerging as central themes for how investors assess the platform’s growth potential and resilience. Now we’ll examine how Oppenheimer’s confidence in Airbnb’s hotel expansion and AI-powered search may influence the company’s existing investment narrative.

Capitalize on the AI infrastructure supercycle with our selection of the 38 best 'picks and shovels' of the AI gold rush converting record-breaking demand into massive cash flow.

Airbnb Investment Narrative Recap

To own Airbnb, you need to believe its platform can keep attracting hosts and guests even as regulations, competition, and travel shocks evolve. Right now, the key near term catalyst is whether Q1 2026 results confirm the earnings and revenue growth analysts are expecting, and Oppenheimer’s upgrade reinforces that focus rather than changing it. The biggest immediate risk is still regulatory and political pressure on short term rentals, and this latest news does not materially change that.

Among recent developments, Airbnb’s 2026 FIFA World Cup partnership stands out as most relevant to Oppenheimer’s upgrade. The event concentrates demand in 16 cities, which aligns with the firm’s view that Airbnb’s distributed inventory and AI powered search can channel large spikes in travel interest. For investors watching near term catalysts, how the platform performs around big tentpole events like the World Cup is becoming an important proof point for the growth story.

title: McDonald's earnings, Fed commentary, labor data: What to Watch
content:
Asking for a Trend Host Josh Lipton previews several of the biggest stories to come tomorrow, Thursday, May 7, including earnings results from McDonald's (MCD), Shell (SHEL), Airbnb (ABNB), CoreWeave (CRWV), and Coinbase (COIN); comments from several Federal Reserve presidents; and this week's reading on initial jobless claims.

Video Transcript

00:05 Speaker A

Time now for what to watch Thursday, May 7th.

00:09 Speaker A

Investors getting a fresh read on the consumer, crypto, and other quarterly earnings reports including Shell, Airbnb, CoreWeave and Lyft.

00:17 Speaker A

McDonald's also reporting on Thursday, company announcing first quarter results.

00:21 Speaker A

Analyst expecting US same store sales to rise up to 4%, driven by easy comps after last year's E coli related slowdown.

00:27 Speaker A

01:06 Speaker A

And finally, we're getting weekly initial jobless claims data on Thursday.

01:10 Speaker A

Economists forecasting claims to tick up to 205,000, giving us more insight into the health of the labor market.

title: Coinbase lays off 14% of workforce, CEO explains AI pivot in memo
content:
Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase Global (COIN) will be cutting 14% of its workforce, according to a new memo out from founder-CEO Brian Armstrong.

Morning Brief Host Julie Hyman and Yahoo Finance Head of News Myles Udland dive into Armstrong's memo and the shift toward making the company more "AI-native."

Coinbase is currently scheduled to release first quarter earnings results this Thursday, May 7.

Video Transcript

00:00 Speaker A

Let's start with Coinbase because that to me is the more interesting announcement. And Brian Armstrong, the CEO of Coinbase just pulled it all out there. He he posted the memo that he had sent to the staff um on his ex account. And so I I want to give um Brian Armstrong props on a couple of fronts. First of all, he says that they're cutting the the company's staff by 14%.

00:23 Speaker A

Um, and I want to give him props for posting the memo, like just doing it straight out. It's on there. And second of all, he didn't say that AI was the primary reason that the cuts are happening. He acknowledges the turmoil, the volatility that has been going on in the crypto market and the volatility that causes internally for the company. Then he says, oh yeah, and AI sort of allows us to make these cuts right now. But but I think like it's important

00:41 Speaker A

when we're talking, you know, the the term AI washing is thrown around, right? That companies are using this as an excuse that he doesn't seem to be doing that. He seems to be, you know, at least acknowledging that there are some underlying challenges in the business because of what's going on in the crypto market.

00:53 Speaker B

Yes. Um, I mean I yeah, AI washing is a strong term. Um, but I I I think I think to me, uh, when I read the memo, I I I'm looking at it now. so forgive my eyes. Um, the what this means section to me felt like the crux of what not only Coinbase is doing, but what a lot of other companies in tech either have done or I think are going to do. And the first

1:12 Speaker B

bullet here, fewer layers, faster decisions. And I'll read from the memo, flattening our org structure to five layers max below CEO COO. And it's interesting that I read that uh this morning because this morning I went on a walk and listened to an interview with Brian Chesky who was Brian Armstrong's boss at one point, talking about Airbnb's own changes in management structures over time. Chesky of course, um kind of the the center of what's now known as founder mode. I think Brian Armstrong very much

1:33 Speaker B

operating in that context and in that interview, talking about, you know, there's the old cliche that the Catholic Church has existed for 2,000 years with four layers of management. Um, so I think to to see this as the sentence. And again, those those guys, you know, Brian Armstrong was an early employee at Airbnb. They go back a long way those two. I think there's a lot of mind meld in terms of how to run organizations. I mean Coinbase and Airbnb um came public in the same year. They have a lot of similar trajectories

1:54 Speaker B

as businesses and I'm not I'm not meaning to make this about Airbnb, but I just think that that approach again in this section of fewer layers, faster decisions, no pure managers, AI native pods. The the current thing as it were, I feel like around how you staff a business like this, a business like Coinbase where you have clearly won a major market right now, like the first 10 years of your company's existence, you are the winner. So now the question is

2:19 Speaker B

what new markets emerge over the next 10 years and how do you win X number of those to the same magnitude that you sort of won this, you know, crypto, or this trading custody like action platform part of crypto, like that 1.0 part. And the real focus right now it seems from a number of these companies is about how you structure yourself to transition from that era to the new one.
